events.title: Proposed ruling: escalate (model confidence 0.93)
events.body:
The complaint filed by the rider is an express dangerous-driving allegation: "speeding and braking hard the whole way, overtaking on the shoulder" and "I was scared and felt unsafe" [F6]. SAFE-2 requires escalation whenever a case involves dangerous-driving allegations, and the policy execution trace records the SAFE-1 safety-incident screen as passed with "allowed outcomes: escalate" [SAFE-2][SAFE-1]. Both advocates independently read the complaint the same way and both requested escalate [F6][SAFE-2]; the driver's advocate resists only a finding of fault, not the escalation.

What happened, fixed by the record: pickup 21:22 and drop-off 21:34 on a RydeX Jurong East MRT → NUS trip [F1]. The GPS record shows 8.3 km actually driven against an 8.4 km optimal route (-0.1 km, -1%) and 12.7 min against a 13.8 min estimate (-1.1 min) [F1][F2]. These facts settle route and total time only; they carry no speed, braking, acceleration or shoulder-use telemetry, so they neither corroborate nor refute the manner-of-driving account and cannot by themselves resolve it [F1][F2][SAFE-2].

The chat record is complete and every message is timestamped: two messages at 21:17 (rider at the taxi stand in a red cap) and 21:18 (driver 4 min away in a blue Prius), both about the meeting point, neither raising any safety concern [F3][F4][F5]. The driver's post-trip statement "I drove normally" and his claim that the rider was on the phone and never complained is a statement, not a system record, and under the record rules does not outweigh the filed complaint; it is also not a positive answer to the manner-of-driving allegation [F6][SAFE-2].

Profiles settle nothing here: rider 1187 days, rating 4.6, 0 disputes and 0 upheld in 90 days; driver 675 days, rating 4.85, 963 trips, 0 disputes and 0 upheld in 90 days [F7][F8]. No profile fact decides the case, and with zero upheld disputes there is no RD-6 predicate for any account flag on either side [F7][F8][RD-6].

The dispute is a safety case and the manner of driving is undetermined on the paper record, so no automated ruling issues; the reviewer should check what telemetry, if any, exists for the 21:22–21:34 window, whether the rider reported the incident through RydeHELP, and whether the driver's account and the rider's complaint can be reconciled [F1][F2][F6][SAFE-2]. No amount is computed, since the fare is a fixed RydeX quote of $20.85 and no fare or add-on fact records an overcharge tied to the allegation [F1][F2][FARE-1]; the complaint is a safety matter, not a fare dispute [SAFE-2].

claims.assertion: The rider's complaint states the driver was 'speeding and braking hard the whole way, overtaking on the shoulder' and that the rider 'was scared and felt unsafe' — an express dangerous-driving allegation that must be screened under SAFE-2.

The ride was taken in the dark (pickup 21:22, drop-off 21:34) and the driver's only written response is his own denial plus an unverifiable claim that the rider was on the phone and 'never complained to me' — a statement about the rider's silence, which does not answer the manner-of-driving allegation.

The GPS record is neutral on driving manner: actual distance 8.3 km against an 8.4 km optimal route (-0.1 km, -1%) and a 12.7 min duration against a 13.8 min estimate show no route deviation and no duration anomaly, so the record neither corroborates nor refutes the complaint and cannot resolve a dangerous-driving allegation on its own.

The chat record is short but complete and timestamped (two messages, 21:17 and 21:18, both about the meeting point), so no in-app message was suppressed and there is no chat-based corroboration of the rider's safety complaint; completeness itself is what allows a human reviewer to proceed on the rider's statement rather than dismissing the case for missing evidence.

The rider (1187-day account, rating 4.6, 0 disputes in 90 days) is not a serial complainant, and the driver's clean 90-day sheet (963 trips, 0 disputes, 0 upheld, F8) cuts both ways: it neither excuses the alleged manner of driving nor supplies the missing evidence, which is why this must go to a person rather than be auto-decided.

weaknesses: The complaint is an uncorroborated narrative: no GPS speed, harsh-braking or acceleration facts exist in the record and no traffic/weather facts were returned for this case, so the dangerous-driving allegation rests on the rider's own words (F6) and the judge may find it unproven on the paper record.

The chat record contains only two messages, both about the meeting point (F3, F4); the rider raised no safety concern at any point during or after the trip, and the driver's statement that the rider 'never complained to me' (F6) is consistent with the chat being silent on driving manner.

The GPS facts actually run slightly in the driver's favour on route and time (F1: 8.3 km vs 8.4 km optimal; F2: 12.7 min vs 13.8 min estimate), so no deviation or delay can be used as circumstantial support for the speeding claim.
The driver's profile (F8: 963 trips in 90 days, rating 4.85, 0 disputes, 0 upheld) will be cited by the other side as character evidence that he drives safely.

claims.assertion: The rider's complaint is a dangerous-driving allegation ('speeding', 'braking hard', 'overtaking on the shoulder', 'I was scared and felt unsafe'), so the case must go to a person rather than an automated ruling.

The GPS record undercuts the speeding allegation: actual distance 8.3 km is 0.1 km (-1%) shorter than the optimal 8.4 km, so no extra ground was covered, and the trip took 12.7 min against the 13.8 min estimate, an ordinary direct run for a RydeX Jurong East MRT to NUS trip.

The chat record is complete and every message is timestamped (2 messages: rider 'I'm at the taxi stand outside the MRT already' at 21:17, driver '4 min away, blue Toyota Prius' at 21:18), and it contains no complaint, no request to slow down and no mention of unsafe driving at any point.

Neither profile supports the allegation or any account action: the rider has 0 disputes in 90 d and 0 upheld, and the driver has 963 trips in 90 d, rating 4.85, 0 disputes and 0 upheld, so there is no repeated-violation record against this driver.
The ticket shows a fixed RydeX charge of $20.85 and no fare or add-on fact in this case records an overcharge tied to the alleged driving, so no refund amount is computable from the record.

weaknesses: The driver's only direct answer is his own post-trip statement 'I drove normally' (F6); it is a claim, not a system record, and the rider's account is likewise an untested statement, so the manner of driving is not positively proved either way.

There is no speed, braking or acceleration telemetry in the record (F1 and F2 carry only distance and duration), so the record cannot positively disprove hard braking or shoulder overtaking — the judge may treat the speeding allegation as undetermined rather than disproved.

Finishing 1.1 min under the estimate (F2) is equally consistent with faster-than-optimal driving, so the other side will use F2 to argue the driver made up time rather than that he drove conservatively.

The rider raised the safety concern in the complaint while never raising it in chat (F3-F5); the other side may explain that silence by the rider being on the phone the whole trip (F6) and too frightened to speak up mid-ride.

points.response: Conceded — both sides read the complaint ('speeding', 'braking hard', 'overtaking on the shoulder', 'I was scared and felt unsafe', F6) as a dangerous-driving allegation, so SAFE-2 sends the case to a person with a fact summary and no automated ruling.

F1 and F2 say nothing about manner of driving: a direct route (8.3 km vs 8.4 km, F1) is equally consistent with driving that route too fast, and finishing 1.1 min under the estimate (F2) is as consistent with aggressive driving as with a smooth run — the record is silent on speed, not exculpatory.

Rider silence in a two-message chat confined to the meeting point (F3, F4; completeness only at F5) is not consent to the driving and not a withdrawal of the complaint; the driver's own explanation of that silence rests on his untested statement that the rider was on the phone (F6), which under the record rules does not outweigh the rider's filed complaint.

The rider does not seek any account action against the driver: F7 and F8 show zero upheld disputes on both sides, so no RD-6 flag_account is requested and the profiles cut neither way on the safety question.

The rider is not asking for money: the RydeX fare is a fixed quote (ticket $20.85) and no fare facts were returned for this case, so the correct relief is an escalated fact summary for human handling, not a refund; the human reviewer should also note the rider's 30-day complaint window under NS-7 if any fee relief is later considered.

Conceded as framed: the complaint text is an express dangerous-driving allegation, so on my own reading it triggers the SAFE-2 screen and the case goes to a person rather than an automated finding; I do not resist escalation, I only resist any finding of fault.

The darkness of the trip (pickup 21:22, drop-off 21:34 as recorded in the case framing) is not itself unsafe driving, and the rider's statement that he was scared was never tested in the only channel the platform provides: the complete chat record (F3 rider 21:17, F4 driver 21:18, F5 all timestamped) carries no request to slow down.

Partly conceded: the record has no speed or braking telemetry, so F1 and F2 cannot decisively resolve manner of driving; but they are not neutral in the driver's favour either — 8.3 km actually driven against 8.4 km optimal (-1%) and 12.7 min against a 13.8 min estimate excludes the classic corroborators of a 'speeding the whole way' account, namely extra ground covered or a squeezed run.

The completeness of the chat record (F5) is exactly what limits the rider: nothing in F3 or F4 records a mid-trip safety protest, and the only competing account of the ride is the driver's contemporaneous-plus-post-trip position in F6, so the paper record contains no evidence of the alleged manner of driving.

Agreed that no profile fact decides this case and that a human reviewer should look at it; F7 and F8 show no prior incident on either side, so there is no repeated-violation record against this driver (963 trips, 0 disputes, 0 upheld in 90 d) and no basis for any account flag.
